summary: A new request joins the running batch at the next schedule() (running pass first, then waiting admission). A request that stops on EOS is freed in update_from_output and reported in the next step's finished_req_ids. Outcome and path (allocate-slots order and status, free) reproduced.

The deployed budget is 8192 (vllm serve on an H100, arg_utils.py:2933-2941), so a 5000-token prompt prefills in one step. With --max-num-batched-tokens 2048, running requests are served first and the prompt gets 2047/2047/906 with one decode running. The model reproduces both cases and the order.
Deployed max_num_seqs is 1024, not 128. With max_num_seqs 2, the third request waits even with token budget left (the max_num_seqs break fires twice) and is admitted once a running request finishes.

The second request adopts the 32 cached blocks (num_computed_tokens 512) and computes only its own 60 tokens. Blocks are cached at allocation, so a same-step hit also works. A prompt equal to the 512-token prefix hits only 496 (capped at num_tokens-1).

FCFS preempts running[-1]. Its blocks are freed, num_computed_tokens is set to 0, it is prepended to waiting, and no waiting request is admitted that step. It is recomputed, with no swap. On resume it reuses its surviving cached blocks (48 tokens, after its tail block was evicted). The model matches the code exactly.

Requests hold ceil(n/16) blocks. On finish, only full hashed blocks stay cached (LRU tail, evictable). The partial last block is uncached and goes to the front of the free queue (LIFO). The model reproduces the free-queue order, the reuse of the cached blocks and the LIFO reuse.

Outcome right: no lookup, full recompute, no block reuse. Path wrong: the model still hashes prompt blocks (code: no block_hasher unless caching is on, core.py:231-238), and its async update-from-output calls full-attention-manager.cache-blocks without the enable_caching guard (kv_cache_manager.py:782-792), so block-pool.cached fills while caching is off.

Priority admission follows (priority, arrival). Under memory pressure the victim is max(priority, arrival) wherever it sits in running (lo is preempted, not the last-running hi), and its scheduled tokens are returned. Only a running request's failed allocation preempts. Self-preemption ends the running pass. All reproduced.
